details.publicNotes:
On rare occasions, a magical conjunction draws a living being into a parallel reality where it should not exist. These unfortunate creatures are forever marked by their transition. Most are soon parted from their physical bodies, becoming immortal astral beings with no place in their new realm's metaphysical cycle of life and death.

Though returning to their own reality is nearly impossible, some dedicate themselves to research on a way to return, while others actively participate in the affairs of their new home, constantly searching for new opportunities. This involvement might be well-intentioned, with the parallel present offering magic, technology, and wisdom from their old reality. On the other hand, parallel presents can just as easily exploit others in the service of their goals. Regardless of their motivations, a parallel present's knowledge isn't perfect, which can lead to undesirable outcomes and attract the attention of aeons, who believe that parallel presents represent an existential threat to reality.

Temporal paradoxes are a rare category of spirits that arise when strong-willed individuals are separated from their rightful place in the timeline. Though they retain strong memories and emotional connections to their pasts, it is seldom possible for them to go back to where they came from. Even if they were to manage the daunting task of locating their original reality and timeline, it would fundamentally reject their return. This rejection stems from a combination of their former realities editing them out in the interest of self-stabilization and the influence of their new realities causing their old homes to recognize them as incompatible invaders. Unfortunately for temporal paradoxes, their new realities don't fully accept them either, making them vulnerable to unwelcome twists of fate.

Don't You Know Me?

Parallel realities can diverge greatly from one another, and two people who are friends or lovers in one reality might be strangers or bitter enemies in another. When an exile from an alternate reality finds that their loved ones no longer love them back, they might refuse to accept this reality, trying to force a relationship where none exists. This imperils not only the people involved but also the host plane, threatening to rupture the thin membrane between realities.

The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.

You manifest a bubble of distorted time. The bubble is filled with tiny pockets where time runs slightly faster or slightly slower than normal. Movement through these temporal pockets is dangerous and disorienting, as muscles and bones slide out of sync with each other. Creatures that enter or begin their turn in the area must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} until it leaves the spell's area.

Failure The creature is clumsy 2 until it leaves the spell's area. While it remains in the area, whenever it uses a move or manipulate action, it takes 6d8 slashing damage with a basic Reflex save.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} until it leaves the spell's area.

Heightened (+1) The damage for using move or manipulate actions increases by 1d8.

You conjure up a wall of slowed time, which is both transparent and sepia-colored. The wall is 1 inch thick, up to 120 feet long, and up to 20 feet high. You can shape the wall's path, placing each 5 feet of the wall on the border between squares. The wall doesn't need to stand vertically or be supported by any surface. You must conjure the wall in an unbroken open space so its edges don't pass through any creatures or objects, or the spell is lost.

Mindless creatures, unattended objects (including thrown weapons and ammunition), and spell effects that pass through the wall are trapped within, emerging 1 round after they enter it. Held objects that enter the wall, such as a melee weapon used to Strike a creature on the other side of the wall, become stuck for 1 round as well. The creature can choose to drop the held object; if they do, the object continues its trajectory after it is freed from the wall's effect; this would allow a melee weapon to resolve the Strike before falling to the ground. However, attacks and targeted effects whose targets have moved from their original position since they entered the wall automatically miss.

Non-mindless creatures that enter the wall of time lose one action from their current turn if they can; if they can't, either because they are on their final action for the turn or it is not their turn, they are instead @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1}.

You push into the target's mind and daze it with a mental jolt. The jolt deals 1d6 mental damage, with a basic Will save. If the target critically fails the save, it is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d6.

You pull an echo of your target's recent injuries through time, inflicting them anew. Choose a type of damage that the target has taken since the beginning of your last turn. The target takes 2d6 damage of that type.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

target.value: 1 creature that has taken damage since the beginning of your last turn

description.value: A parallel present takes additional damage from attacks whose attack roll was altered by a fortune effect.
The parallel present senses all non-mindless creatures in the listed range.

Trigger The parallel present is targeted by a Strike while they have at least one duplicate

Effect The parallel present and the duplicate swap places. The triggering Strike resolves against the duplicate instead.

The parallel present vanishes and reappears 10 feet away in a random direction, gaining 10 temporary Hit Points. Any duplicates of the parallel present also vanish and reappear in random directions. This effect can't cause the parallel present or their duplicates to enter hazardous terrain or an occupied space.

The parallel present's condensed timeline anchors its targets to the present moment. A creature that is critically hit by the parallel present's timeline strike is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1}.

The parallel present creates two duplicates in spaces adjacent to themselves. These duplicates have the same AC and saving throw modifiers as the parallel present but disappear if they take any damage. While a duplicate exists, the parallel present can roll twice and take the better result on any Strike or saving throw (unless all duplicates had to roll a saving throw against the effect). If they do, a duplicate of their choice is destroyed after the attack roll or saving throw is resolved; they can't select a duplicate that also had to roll a saving throw. The duplicates mirror the parallel present's motions but do not move from the space where they were created except by Flickering Form. A creature that Seeks can identify a parallel present as real or a duplicate with a successful @Check[perception|dc:35] check. The parallel present can have at most six duplicates. Duplicates disappear after 1 minute.

Requirements The parallel present has at least one duplicate

Effect The parallel present vanishes and reappears adjacent to a creature within 20 feet. Any number of the parallel present's duplicates also vanish and reappear adjacent to the target creature. The parallel present attempts a timeline Strike against the target creature, gaining an additional die of damage for each duplicate adjacent to the target creature.
